t: Toronto police AI plate readers draw "constant eyes" warning
s: CBC covers the fully deployed fleet: every marked cruiser scans plates, makes and models. TPS 2026 budget adds $5.6M for "AI Operationalization."

t: ALPR quietly expanding across Canada — without Flock
s: Ottawa grew 5→65 equipped vehicles; Sudbury added 16 fixed sites; Waterloo went live in June. Flock confirms zero Canadian police partnerships; the OPP says it has no plans to use them.

t: Supreme Court: geofence data is a Fourth Amendment search
s: Chatrie v. US (6-3) — widely read as a legal time bomb for ALPR dragnets. The Norfolk Flock case is at the Fourth Circuit.

t: Washington signs the Driver Privacy Act
s: 21-day retention cap, immigration-enforcement ban, no cameras near schools, courts, or places of worship.
Denver removed all 110 Flock cameras (then bought a smaller Axon network over ACLU objections). NPR counts contract cancellations nationwide — even as Flock crosses 100,000 total cameras.

t: Researchers find Flock camera feeds exposed online
s: 60+ live camera feeds and debug interfaces open to the internet with no password; 50+ vulnerabilities; stolen customer credentials on crime forums. Cited by several cities in cancellations.

t: California sues El Cajon over plate-data sharing
s: AG Bonta: sharing ALPR data with 100+ out-of-state agencies violates SB 34.

t: Illinois audit: Flock let CBP into state cameras
s: Trigger: a Texas deputy searched 83,000 cameras nationwide for a woman who self-administered an abortion — hitting Illinois. Evanston and Oak Park terminated contracts.
First major-city cancellation, after organizers surfaced the ICE search revelations. Texas DPS later installed its own readers in the city over local objections.

t: 404 Media: police ran ~4,000 Flock searches for ICE
s: Despite ICE having no Flock contract. Separate reporting: CBP had quiet access to 80,000+ cameras via an undisclosed pilot. The story that started the backlash.

t: Flock builds "Nova" people-lookup on breach data
s: Leaked audio: jumping "from LPR to person" using data brokers and hacked datasets, no warrant. Flock said it dropped the breach data after internal objections; later analysis disputed that.
Every marked vehicle scans at up to 225 km/h — 1.25M+ plate reads/day capacity. Reads kept 7 days, hits 365.
